description:
Scholarship Overview

The DAAD EPOS (Development-Related Postgraduate Courses) Scholarship is a , fully funded opportunity offered by the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) for international students from developing and emerging countries. This scholarship supports master's and doctoral studies in development-related fields at participating German universities. The EPOS program specifically targets future leaders who will contribute to the development of their home countries through the knowledge and expertise gained in Germany.

Financial Benefits & Coverage

  • Monthly stipend: €992 for Master's programs; €1,300 for PhD programs.
  • Health, accident, and personal liability insurance.
  • Travel allowance (round-trip airfare to Germany).
  • Study/research subsidy.
  • German language course funding (optional).
  • Family subsidy and possible rent subsidy.
  • Accommodation assistance.
  • No application fee; fully funded.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Citizen of a developing or emerging country (list on DAAD website).
  • Four-year bachelor's degree or equivalent in a relevant subject.
  • At least two years of relevant professional experience (typically required, exceptions may apply).
  • Applying for a development-related master's or PhD program at a participating German university.
  • Demonstrate how studies will contribute to home country development.
  • English proficiency: IELTS not required, but must demonstrate sufficient proficiency through previous English-medium education or alternative tests.

Application Process

  1. Research eligible EPOS-supported programs on the DAAD database.
  2. Check university-specific requirements.
  3. Prepare required documents: DAAD application form, CV, letter of motivation, letter of recommendation, academic certificates, language proficiency proof, work experience certificates, research proposal (for PhD), passport copy, photo.
  4. Submit university application directly to the chosen German university.
  5. Apply for DAAD EPOS scholarship through the DAAD portal.
  6. Wait for selection results (typically June–September).
  7. Accept scholarship and prepare for Germany.

Participating Universities (Examples)

  • Heidelberg University
  • TU Dresden
  • University of Freiburg
  • Humboldt University Berlin
  • University of Bonn
  • RWTH Aachen University

Full list available on DAAD database.

Timeline & Deadlines

MilestoneDate
Application opensOctober/November (previous year)
Application deadline15 May (for following academic year)
University reviewJune–July
DAAD evaluationJuly–August
NotificationSeptember
Program startOctober–March

Official Link

https://www.daad.de/en/study-and-research-in-germany/scholarships/development-related-postgraduate-courses/

Important Notes

  • The 2026/27 intake deadline (15 May 2026) has passed. Next cycle expected to open October/November 2026 with deadline 15 May 2027.
  • IELTS/TOEFL not mandatory but proof of English proficiency required.
  • Scholarship is for development-related courses only; not all German university programs are eligible.
  • DAAD expects scholars to return to home countries after completion.
